mechanism.statement: Observed per-token posthoc delta-channel concentration and poor common-channel support may coexist with a lower-dimensional common output-function basis in which each token has different coefficients. This is a competing representation hypothesis, not a measured Wan result.
mechanism.math_or_trace: For token block B, ΔU_r=V_t Δq_r; define μ_B=mean_r ΔU_r and e_r=ΔU_r−μ_B, giving Σ_r||ΔU_r||²=|B| ||μ_B||²+Σ_r||e_r||². The decomposition is exact; a cheap rank-k predictor or executable factorization for e_r has not been established.

availability.observer_computation: Computing Δq for current steps requires full W1/GELU/Q2; any early function-basis observer would have additional work.

real_cost.W2: No executed reduction; output-space basis must account for transforms

evidence.scope: Six exposed sources, saved32 row analysis, five sampled blocks, 25% posthoc delta value diagonal innovation SSE 2.44%–7.07%
Two exposed sources, original raster M128 tiles, common-innovation energy first/last layers greater than sampled middle layers; shared 25% diagonal SSE ~39%–42% middle

countermechanism.statement: The observed shared-support loss is intrinsic high-dimensional token-specific function variation, not merely a poor original hidden basis.
countermechanism.prediction: Conditional output-space low-dimensional shared basis will not improve matched-data reconstruction vs suitably matched per-token and shared-column baselines once independent tokens and selector costs are included.

discriminator: Use existing two-source contiguous saved Δq and W2/gate: compare matched-rank output subspace (with held-out token/source basis fitting) vs shared-column, fixed, and shuffled controls. Evaluate signed function reconstruction per token plus source-held-out generality before considering early predictor or new native jobs.
